request.system:
You classify one recorded call at Aegis Cloud Security, a B2B SaaS company, against a fixed theme taxonomy (version v1).

You receive the full transcript as numbered turns in the form "[index] Speaker (side): sentence". side is "customer" (works at an outside company) or "aegis_staff" (works at Aegis). You are given nothing else about the call: no title, no call type, no summary. Judge only from the words in the transcript.

THEMES (what kind of conversation it is; pick by what the call is mostly about):
1. Commercial Renewals and Retention: Renewals, contracts, pricing and SLA negotiation, churn risk, expansion deals. Boundary: If a call is mainly about product adoption with renewal as an aside, use Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion.
2. Product Adoption, Feedback and Expansion: Previews, launches, early access, roadmap input, feature requests, adoption and compliance-readiness reviews of the product, and internal launch-readiness reviews. Boundary: The module belongs in the product area field, not in the theme. Renewal talk that is only an aside stays here.
3. Incident and Outage Response: War rooms, root cause, remediation plans, customer impact assessment, incident communication, postmortems, reliability reviews. Boundary: A single customer's technical fault that is not a platform incident belongs in Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
4. Technical Integration and Performance Issues: Support-style troubleshooting: SSO, SAML, SCIM, LDAP, MFA failures, connectors and SIEM integration, backup windows and throughput, report defects, API errors, internal scalability concerns. Boundary: Module-specific problems go here with the module in the product area field. A platform-wide outage is Incident and Outage Response.
5. Onboarding and Implementation Scoping: Kickoffs, deployment planning, architecture scoping, setup workshops. Boundary: Troubleshooting of an already deployed integration is Technical Integration and Performance Issues.
6. Billing and Usage Disputes: Invoices, overages, seat counts, billing adjustments. Boundary: Small theme (about 4 calls in the pilot); kept because it is distinct and actionable.
7. Competitive Strategy and Win/Loss: Competitive intelligence, battlecards, win/loss analysis, and customer-facing calls where the customer is evaluating alternatives. Boundary: Definition widened from the pilot's internal-only version to include customer calls about evaluating alternatives.
8. Internal Planning and Delivery Cadence: Standups, sprint planning, retros, all-hands, design and roadmap syncs with no customer or incident focus. Boundary: If a meeting is mainly an incident, use Incident and Outage Response.

Other / new theme: use only if no theme above fits. Then describe the call in one sentence in other_description. Other / new theme only if no theme fits. More than 10% of calls in Other triggers a taxonomy revision (new version, full re-run).

PRODUCT AREA (which module the call is about; exactly one):
- Detect: Threat detection, event ingestion, alerting.
- Comply: Compliance reporting and evidence mapping (including Comply v2).
- Protect: Backup, snapshots, disaster recovery (includes backup).
- Identity: Directory sync, SSO, SAML, SCIM, MFA, IAM governance.
- Platform/General: No single product dominates, or the call is cross-product.

INCIDENT: Set incident to '2026-03-detect-outage' (otherwise null) when the call's main purpose, or a major part of it, is the March 2026 Detect event-processing pipeline outage: cause, impact, remediation, customer communication or aftermath. A separate field so the outage story is visible across support, external and internal calls.

Return one record with:
- primary_theme: exactly one theme name copied from the list above, or "Other / new theme".
- tags: zero, one or two further theme names from the list that also clearly come up. Never repeat the primary theme. Empty when primary_theme is "Other / new theme".
- product_area: exactly one product area name copied from the list.
- incident: "2026-03-detect-outage" or null.
- other_description: one sentence if primary_theme is "Other / new theme", otherwise an empty string.
- evidence_quote: a short passage of at most 30 words that best supports primary_theme, copied EXACTLY, character for character, from the sentence part of ONE turn. Copy only the words after "Speaker (side): ". Never include the index, the speaker name, the side or the colon prefix. Do not paraphrase, do not shorten with "...", do not join text from different turns.
- confidence: "high" if clearly about the primary theme, "medium" if two themes compete, "low" if it fits poorly.
- taxonomy_version: "v1".

Return only JSON matching the schema.

[3] Lauren Bishop (customer): That works. And I do have some things I want to flag, so... yeah, let's just get into it.
[4] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Of course. Why don't you go first actually — what's on your mind?
[5] Lauren Bishop (customer): Okay, so the big thing — and I want to be direct here — is the outage in March. The Detect outage. That was... that was not a great experience for us.
[6] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Yeah, and I completely understand. I was going to bring that up myself. That was March 10th through roughly the 18th, the event processing issue — six hours of no visibility on threat monitoring.
[7] Lauren Bishop (customer): Right. And look, I get that outages happen, I've been in infrastructure long enough to know nothing is bulletproof, but six hours is a long time. Our security team was basically flying blind.
[8] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Completely fair. And I don't want to just gloss over it with a, you know, 'here's what we did to fix it' kind of answer if you have more to say about the impact on your side.
[9] Lauren Bishop (customer): I mean, we didn't have an incident during that window, which is lucky, but it surfaced a gap in our own contingency planning too, so it wasn't all on Aegis. It just... it raised questions internally about the reliability of the platform.
[10] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): That's really helpful context, and I appreciate you being candid about it. On our end, the root cause was a single point of failure in the event ingestion pipeline — it was a cascading failure from there. Engineering has since deployed redundant processing nodes and implemented a circuit breaker pattern, so the architecture is fundamentally different now in that layer.
[11] Lauren Bishop (customer): Okay. Is there documentation on that? Like, something I can actually share with my team rather than just taking your word for it?
[12] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Yes, absolutely. We put out a full post-incident review — I'll send that over after the call. It goes into the root cause analysis, the remediation steps, and the testing we did before re-deploying.
[13] Lauren Bishop (customer): Good. That'll help. My team wants to see that it's not just a band-aid.
[14] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Understood. And honestly if there are follow-up questions after your team reviews it, I can also set up time with one of our solution architects to walk through the technical details.
[15] Lauren Bishop (customer): That might be worth doing, yeah. Let me see what the team thinks after they read the doc. Okay, so that's the main concern. What else — you said you wanted to cover the renewal specifically?
[16] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Right. So your current contract runs through end of June, so we're about... eleven weeks out. I wanted to start the conversation early so we're not scrambling in June.
[17] Lauren Bishop (customer): Smart. Yeah. What are you looking at — is pricing changing?
[18] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): So, there is a standard escalator built into the contract — I believe it's three percent — and that would apply. But I also want to understand what your scope looks like going into next year before we lock anything in, because if you're expanding, that changes the conversation.
[19] Lauren Bishop (customer): Mm. Yeah, so we're planning to add about forty more cloud workloads through Q3 as we finish migrating the last of our on-prem stuff. So the footprint is growing.
[20] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Okay, that's good to know. Are those workloads going to be on CloudPrime primarily, or is it a mix?
[21] Lauren Bishop (customer): Mix. Mostly CloudPrime, some Azure — we've got about a 70/30 split right now and I think it stays roughly there.
[22] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Got it. That's helpful. So I'll put together some options — probably a base renewal at your current tier, and then a growth option that prices in that expanded workload count. I can model out what makes sense financially for both sides.
[23] Lauren Bishop (customer): That'd be useful. And, um, I do want to flag — we're not exclusively evaluating Aegis. I have procurement pushing me to get at least one competitive quote, so... I want to be transparent about that.
[24] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): I appreciate you being upfront. Who are you looking at, if you don't mind me asking?
[25] Lauren Bishop (customer): Probably SentinelShield, just because they've been pretty aggressive in our space lately. I don't have a strong pull toward them but procurement wants the comparison.
[26] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Fair enough. I'll make sure our proposal is competitive on value, not just price. And I'm happy to do a side-by-side if that would be helpful for your internal review.
[27] Lauren Bishop (customer): Maybe. Let me see what SentinelShield comes back with first.
[28] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Of course. Just know the offer is there. Okay, I also wanted to touch on Comply v2 — you're currently on Comply, right? The new version just went GA on April 7th.
[29] Lauren Bishop (customer): Oh yeah, I saw the release notes. The on-demand reporting — we've actually already poked around in it a little.
[30] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Oh great, any early impressions?
[31] Lauren Bishop (customer): It's... decent. The SOC 2 report generation is noticeably faster than v1. We haven't dug into the HIPAA or ISO stuff yet because that's not really our priority, but the multi-framework view is something we'll probably use for PCI.
[32] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): That's good to hear on the SOC 2 side — that's been one of the most common things customers come to us about. And yeah, PCI DSS coverage in v2 is pretty robust, so I'd encourage you to test that whenever you get a chance.
[33] Lauren Bishop (customer): We will. Our next PCI audit cycle is Q4 so I want to have that dialed in before then.
[34] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Perfect timing then. I can connect you with our compliance specialist if you want a guided walkthrough before you're in the thick of audit prep.
[35] Lauren Bishop (customer): Yeah, actually, that would be useful. Maybe in June or so.
[36] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): I'll make a note of that. Okay, so to recap what I'm taking away — I'll send the post-incident review for the Detect outage, I'll put together two renewal proposal options with pricing that reflects the expanded workload, and I'll pencil in a compliance walkthrough for sometime in June. Does that cover everything?
[37] Lauren Bishop (customer): I think so. And if we decide to loop in the solutions architect on the Detect stuff, I'll reach out through you.
[38] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Absolutely, just ping me and I'll coordinate. What's a good turnaround for the proposal — does two weeks work, so around the 24th?
[39] Lauren Bishop (customer): Yeah, that's fine. I probably won't get to it until the following week anyway, so that timing works.
[40] Lisa Park (aegis_staff): Perfect. Alright, I'll let you get back to your Q2 planning chaos. Thanks again for the time, Lauren.
[41] Lauren Bishop (customer): Thanks Lisa. Talk soon.
